source.prompt: Which CRMs have a free plan, and what are the limits on it?
source.note: real collected answer; brand, competitors and publishers are the specs the cycle was scored with

answer.text:
Several CRMs offer free plans, each with unique limits on users, contacts, and features—HubSpot, Zoho CRM, Freshsales, EngageBay, Bitrix24, Zite, and Clarify are the top options.
1. HubSpot CRM
Users: Unlimited
Contacts: Up to 1 million
Features: Contact and deal management, email tracking (2,000 emails/month), live chat widget, mobile app, basic marketing tools
Limits: HubSpot branding on emails, landing pages, and forms; advanced automation requires a paid plan; workflow automations and AI-powered tools are restricted
Best for: Teams needing all-in-one CRM with marketing capabilities 2
2 Sources
2. Zoho CRM
Users: Up to 3 on the free plan
Contacts/Records: 5,000 records per module
Features: Lead, contact, and deal management, basic workflows, Zia AI assistant for predictions, mobile app access, multichannel marketing integration
Limits: Restrictive user limit; advanced reporting and automation require paid plans
Best for: Very small teams already using Zoho apps 2
2 Sources
3. Freshsales (Freshworks CRM)
Users: Unlimited
Contacts: Unlimited
Features: Built-in phone system, contact and deal management, email and call logging, customer chat functionality
Limits: No workflow automation; AI-powered scoring and sales sequences require paid tiers
Best for: Small sales teams that prioritize unlimited users and built-in calling 2
2 Sources
4. EngageBay
Users: Up to 15
Contacts: 250
Features: CRM + Marketing + Service Desk, live chat, landing page builder, 1,000 email sends/month
Limits: Limited contacts (250), basic automation only, max 5 forms
Best for: Startups needing combined CRM, marketing automation, and support in one free tool 2
2 Sources
5. Bitrix24
Users: Up to 12 (in SelectHub; elsewhere may be higher)
Contacts/Deals: Unlimited
Features: CRM, project management, HR tools, video calls, calendar sync, pipeline tracking, web forms, built-in telephony, mobile app
Limits: One sales pipeline free; limited workflow automation; max 1,000 emails/month; 5 GB storage; navigation can be complex
Best for: Teams needing CRM plus project management and collaboration in one platform 2
2 Sources
6. Zite
Users: Unlimited
Contacts/Records: 5,000 records
Features: Build custom CRM using AI no-code app creation, visual workflows, connect to external tools, client dashboard, unlimited apps
Limits: Free AI credits (50) constrain modifications if used heavily; not pre-built out-of-the-box 1
1 Source
7. Clarify
Users: Unlimited
Credits: 2,500 AI credits/month for tasks
Features: AI-powered automation, core CRM (contact management, deal tracking, sales pipeline), integrations, email support
Limits: AI task credits capped; higher volume usage may require upgrading
Best for: Startups seeking AI-native automation without per-seat costs 1
1 Source
Key Notes on Free CRMs
User Limits: Many free CRMs cap users (Zoho: 3, EngageBay: 15), but some allow unlimited users (HubSpot, Freshsales, Clarify, Zite).
Contact Limits: Ranges from 250 (EngageBay) up to 1 million (HubSpot) or unlimited (Freshsales).
Automation & AI: Workflow automation and advanced AI features are often restricted to paid tiers; some platforms provide limited AI credits or basic triggers.
Feature Constraints: Emails, landing pages, advanced reporting, branding, and integrations may have limitations.
When to upgrade: If the team exceeds user/contact limits, requires advanced workflow automation, custom reporting, or unbranded communications 2
2 Sources
Choosing the Right Free CRM
Define team size, current and projected contacts, and must-have features (AI, built-in calling, marketing).
Test multiple free plans (no credit card), import contacts, and set up pipelines for 1–2 weeks.
Evaluate when scaling will require upgrading to a paid plan.
Free CRMs provide a strong starting point for small teams, startups, and solo entrepreneurs, with HubSpot, Freshsales, and Clarify offering the most generous user capacities, while EngageBay and Zoho suit tightly limited, small teams.
